Section "## Ba quy tắc" holds exactly three numbered rules: "1. **Một lỗi một báo cáo.** Báo cáo gộp ba vấn đề thường được sửa không vấn đề nào."; "2. **Tái hiện nhỏ nhất.** …"; "3. **Phân biệt mức ảnh hưởng và độ ưu tiên.** …". The lesson's second code block byte-compares identical to lines 41-45 of the file at the tag.

Rule 3, lines 44-45: "Mức ảnh hưởng do bạn quan sát; độ ưu tiên do người quản lý sản phẩm quyết định. Đừng tự đặt cả hai." The lesson renders it as "you observe the impact, the person holding the product sets the order of work, and you set only your half", which does not exceed the source.

Rule 2, lines 42-43: "**Tái hiện nhỏ nhất.** Đơn 2 chỉ có một dòng và hiện 0 — chi tiết đó thu hẹp phạm vi hơn cả trang mô tả." The file does name order 2 as the smallest reproduction and does say it narrows the scope more than a page of description.

Definitional against the lesson's own definition in section 3 ("everything a reader needs to produce the same failure themselves, with you not in the room"): a step whose starting state only the reporter can produce cannot be carried out by that reader. No document in versions.yaml governs report writing; none applies.

Definitional: "the actual value alone says what happened and only the expectation says it was wrong" restates what makes a value a defect rather than a datum. No pinned documentation covers report layout, and the lesson claims nothing stronger (it does not say a reader can never infer the expectation).

The inference is stronger than the logic behind it. Removing a factor while the failure stays shows the factor is not required for this reproduction; it does not show the defect cannot live there (a failure with two independent paths survives removal of either). Section 3 states the strong form flatly: "everything you took away is a place the bug is not". The template's rule 2 only claims narrowing: "chi tiết đó thu hẹp phạm vi hơn cả trang mô tả".
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Everything you take away while the failure stays is one thing the failure does not need; a description rules nothing out.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Settled by running the code, not by opinion. TotalVnd loops "for (var i = 0; i < lines.Count - 1; i++)", so with one line the condition is 0 < 0 and no unit price is ever read. Executing `dotnet run --project samples/DonHang.Samples -- wrong-total` at stage-0 printed "one line only: expected 1250000, got 0". A one-line case showing 0 therefore points at how lines are counted, not at any price, and the lesson states it as a pointer only.

Normative statement about readers, hedged in the lesson and grounded in the repository file, whose Nghi ngờ nguyên nhân field demands "ghi rõ đây là phỏng đoán". The lesson asserts no measured effect, only the reason for the label. No document in versions.yaml covers this.

Property of the medium and the lesson claims no more: "a picture gives the reader a number to retype rather than text to paste" — it does not say a screenshot is worthless, and it pairs the point with the missing steps, environment and data. The pinned documentation set has no page on screenshots as evidence; none applies.

Normative, and hedged with the mechanism the lesson names ("the data that produced it has been replaced"). It states no rule about when a defect must be filed and no measured cost. No document in versions.yaml speaks to defect-reporting timing.

Its factual half is carried by the repository file: "Mức ảnh hưởng do bạn quan sát; độ ưu tiên do người quản lý sản phẩm quyết định." The addition ("priority weighs that harm against everything else the team owes") is a definition of prioritising, hedged with "usually". No official document applies.

Attributed and hedged in section 5 ("tends to get none of them fixed"), matching rule 1 verbatim: "Báo cáo gộp ba vấn đề thường được sửa không vấn đề nào." The reason added ("there is no single thing to close") is definitional for a tracker entry closed as a unit. The five-line summary repeats it as "usually", still inside the source's "thường".

Counted row by row in db/seed.sql order_items, rows per order_id: 1->2, 2->1, 3->2, 4->1, 5->2, 6->1, 7->2, 8->1, 9->1, 10->2, 11->1, 12->2. Exactly six orders hold more than one line — 1, 3, 5, 7, 10, 12 — and the other six hold one each. STAGE.md: "**PostgreSQL 17** (`db`) … 8 products, 5 customers (one of whom never ordered), 12 orders." So section 5's "exactly half" and section 7's two sets are right.

Executed, not inferred. Program.cs maps "[\"wrong-total\"] = Sync(WrongTotal.Run),"; WrongTotal.Run hard-codes "{ (1, 1_250_000), (2, 450_000) }". `dotnet run --project samples/DonHang.Samples -- wrong-total` in the stage-0 worktree (dotnet 10.0.300) printed exactly:
"expected 2150000, got 1250000"
"one line only: expected 1250000, got 0".
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang stage-0: samples/DonHang.Samples/Program.cs; Samples/Debug/WrongTotal.cs; command output

issues.text: "everything you took away is a place the bug is not" overstates the shrinking rule. Dropping a factor while the failure stays shows the factor is not needed to reproduce it, not that the defect cannot be there — a failure reachable two ways survives either removal. Section 4 repeats the strong form ("rules that part out"); the repository rule it credits claims only narrowing ("chi tiết đó thu hẹp phạm vi hơn cả trang mô tả").
issues.fix: In section 3 write "everything you took away is one thing the failure does not need", and in section 4 "Everything you take away while the failure stays is one thing the failure does not need". Nothing else changes; the template quote already says only that the detail narrows the scope.
issues.quote: everything you took away is a place the bug is not

issues.text: "the sample data holds other orders to try" invites a run that stage-0 cannot give. Nothing at the tag puts orders 2 or 3 through the faulty total: WrongTotal hard-codes order 1's two lines and a one-line slice of order 1, and the SQL in db/queries sums correctly. Orders 2 and 3 are rows in db/seed.sql and a sentence in the template's evidence line, not cases a reader can execute.
issues.fix: Replace "the sample data holds other orders to try" with "the sample data holds other shapes to compare — order 2 with one line, order 3 with two", so the sentence stays about the data the repository ships and does not promise a run that does not exist at stage-0.
issues.quote: the sample data holds other orders to try — order 2 with one line, order 3 with two

issues.text: Section 7 rests on a general rule of the sample code — the total is short by exactly its last line — that no claim in .meta.json states; claim 22 covers only order 1's hard-coded lines and the one-line case. The rule is true (TotalVnd loops "i < lines.Count - 1"), and section 2 leans on it too ("the total on screen is short by the last line"), so this is a gap in the ledger, not a false sentence.
issues.fix: Add one claim to .meta.json, kind behavior: "At stage-0 WrongTotal.TotalVnd sums every line except the last (loop bound lines.Count - 1), so a multi-line total is short by exactly its last line and a one-line total is 0." source_hint: samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Debug/WrongTotal.cs. No lesson text changes.
issues.quote: every order, since the total drops its last line

issues.text: The key (a) is correct given the lesson, but its wording collides with section 7: "whatever the second line does is not where the bug is" reads against "the total drops its last line", which is precisely the second line of a two-line order. What shrinking actually establishes is that a second line is not needed for the failure, not that the second line is innocent.
issues.fix: Reword option a to "Order 2 has one line and still shows a wrong total, so a second line is not needed to produce the failure", and adjust the correct explanation to match. The answer key stays ["a"].
